nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Light reaching the canopy and forest edges drives growth of the trees and shrubs that feed the whole montane forest.

nodes.name: Montane rainfall and mist
nodes.desc: Frequent rain and cloud on the Congo-Nile divide keep this high-altitude forest moist and growing.

nodes.name: Forest soil and leaf litter
nodes.desc: Fallen leaves and dead wood build a nutrient store that the forest trees draw on again.

nodes.name: Fungi and soil microbes
nodes.desc: Break down dead leaves, wood and animals, returning nutrients to the forest soil.

nodes.name: Maesa
nodes.desc: A common African shrub or small tree of forest edges and clearings. Its berries are eaten by many forest birds.

nodes.name: African holly
nodes.desc: A montane evergreen tree whose fruits are taken by turacos, bulbuls and other forest birds.

nodes.name: Macaranga
nodes.desc: A fast-growing pioneer tree genus of African montane forest; the species here is common in the Kibira area and used for chimpanzee nests.

nodes.name: Tarenna
nodes.desc: A shrubby understorey plant of Afromontane forest whose small fruits are eaten by birds.

nodes.name: Ruwenzori colobus
nodes.desc: A leaf-eating monkey of the park. It also takes fruit and flowers, and its digestion lets it use food other primates cannot.

nodes.name: L'Hoest's monkey
nodes.desc: A forest guenon recorded in Kibira that feeds mostly on fruit and other plant material.

nodes.name: Black-billed turaco
nodes.desc: A fruit-eating forest bird; GloBI records show it eating Ilex mitis and Maesa lanceolata fruits.

nodes.name: Common bulbul
nodes.desc: A common fruit-eating songbird; records show it eating the fruits of Ilex, Macaranga, Maesa and Tarenna.

nodes.name: Yellow-streaked greenbul
nodes.desc: A forest-understorey songbird recorded eating Maesa and Tarenna fruits.

nodes.name: Yellow-rumped tinkerbird
nodes.desc: A small forest barbet recorded eating Maesa and Tarenna fruits.

nodes.name: Jackson's soft-furred mouse
nodes.desc: The most-recorded mammal near the park; an abundant forest floor rodent that eats seeds, fruit and insects.

nodes.name: Forest insects
nodes.desc: Beetles, butterflies, ants and other insects feed on leaves and litter, and in turn feed many small predators.

nodes.name: White-starred robin
nodes.desc: A forest-floor songbird that feeds on insects and also takes fruit such as Ilex and Maesa berries.

nodes.name: Volcano forest shrew
nodes.desc: A small insect-eating mammal of Albertine Rift forest floors, among the more recorded mammals near the park.

nodes.name: African striped skink
nodes.desc: A lizard that hunts insects and is preyed on by snakes.

nodes.name: Olive grass snake
nodes.desc: A slender snake; GloBI records show it eating the African striped skink.

nodes.name: Mountain buzzard
nodes.desc: A raptor of montane forest, listed for Kibira; it hunts small mammals, reptiles and insects from perches.

nodes.name: Eastern chimpanzee
nodes.desc: Kibira holds about 200 eastern chimpanzees. They eat mostly fruit, plus insects, and hunt other monkeys such as colobus.
